b-positive.essence: the shape margin in the packing bound
b-positive.statement: the number b is two times the log of four times the window radius r times the denominator d, a fixed margin strictly above zero depending only on the shape of the window, chosen once before the tower level varies

denom-d.essence: where the norm one set lives, and the separation it forces
denom-d.source_lines: the lattice setup (L295–300), the separation step (L405–420)
denom-d.statement: the norm one set lives in the lattice with denominator d, the square of the product of the split primes, and any nonzero lattice element has some coordinate with modulus at least one over d, since the algebraic integer norm is at least one

gamma-positive.essence: the margin the criterion assumes positive
gamma-positive.statement: the margin gamma is t times the log of 2 minus the log of h, and the criterion takes gamma strictly above zero as a hypothesis; whether such a t against such an h actually happens is the arithmetic half's job, not this statement's

hypo-infinity.essence: the growing degrees the criterion assumes
hypo-infinity.source_lines: the criterion's hypothesis (L375–383), the tower degree (L602–606)
hypo-infinity.statement: the field degrees tend to infinity as the tower level varies, and that is a hypothesis of the criterion; the construction of levels whose degrees grow is the arithmetic half's job

normonecount.essence: the size of the norm one set the window will hold
normonecount.statement: when the t split primes give two to the tf conjugate pair choices and the ideal class group is at most h to the f power, the pigeonhole leaves at least two to the tf over h to the f elements with norm one to the lower field, each of absolute value one under every complex embedding

one-embed-zero.essence: why vanishing in one coordinate marks the zero point
one-embed-zero.statement: a field element that is zero in a single complex embedding is the zero element, because an embedding carries nonzero elements to nonzero numbers

overlap-ratio.essence: the window overlap that the averaging step keeps
overlap-ratio.statement: the overlap of two window discs whose centers differ by one unit translation, as a share of one disc's area, tends to one as the window radius grows, so a radius large enough makes the log of that share above minus gamma over two

slack-compose-rule.source_lines: the fixed constants (L730–740), the absorption step (L455–460)
slack-compose-rule.statement: a positive margin divided by a positive margin is a positive margin, and a fixed half factor in front of a growing power is absorbed for large arguments, so the arithmetic of the margins is the arithmetic of positivity

torus-average.essence: some translate does at least as well as the average
torus-average.statement: averaging over all lattice translates, the expected window points are the window volume over the lattice volume, and the expected kept pairs are the norm one count times the overlap share to the f power times that expectation, so some translate does at least as well as the average

vol-compare.statement: disjoint equal balls packed inside a bigger ball: the number of small balls times the small ball volume is at most the big ball volume

delta-positive.statement: the exponent delta is gamma over four b — a positive margin divided by a positive margin is a positive margin — and the fixed half is absorbed for large n, so for all large n the pair count is at least n to the power one plus delta

growth-compare.statement: the pair count is at least a half of n times e to the gamma f over two; since e to the b f bounds n with b positive, f is at least log n over b, so the pair count is at least a half of n to the power one plus gamma over two b; and n itself is at least e to the gamma f over two, since the pair count is at most n squared

infinity-end.statement: the point counts grow without bound as the tower level varies, so for any proposed cap c over log log n some level drops the cap below delta and the bound fails there: for infinitely many n the unit segments are at least n to the power one plus delta

pack-bound.statement: the window's points are separated by at least one over d in some coordinate, so the point count n is at most (four times the window radius r times the denominator d) to the power two f, which is e to the b f

proj-inj.statement: projecting the window points to the first complex coordinate identifies no two distinct points, so the planar set has the window's point count, and its unit segments are at least a half of e to the gamma f over two times that count

window-rich.statement: some translate of the lattice keeps a rich share: the directed pairs it carries are at least e to the gamma f over two times the points it carries
